6-source-1.title: Best Practices for Event Logging and Threat Detection
6-source-1.publisher: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) in cooperation with ASD's ACSC, FBI, NSA, NCSC-UK, CCCS, NCSC-NZ, NISC, NCSC-Korea, CSA, AIVD, MIVD
6-source-1.applicability: Organizations implementing event logging systems for network visibility and threat detection across cloud services, enterprise networks, operational technology, and mobility with moderate technical complexity

passages.text: Organisations should consider establishing an accurate and trustworthy time source and use this consistently across all systems to assist network defenders in identifying connections between event logs.

An event logging facility should enable the protection of logs from unauthorised modification and deletion. Ensure that only personnel with a justified requirement have permission to delete or modify event logs and view the audit logs for access to the centralised logging environment.

ASD’s ACSC and co-authors recommend that organisations consider implementing user and entity behavioural analytics capabilities to enable automated detection of behavioural anomalies on networks, devices, or accounts. SIEMs can detect anomalous activity by comparing event logs to a baseline of business-as-usual traffic and activity.

6-source-2.title: IBM Z Time Synchronization Implementation Guide
6-source-2.applicability: Organizations requiring high-accuracy time synchronization through standard protocols (NTP, PTP, PPS) for log integrity in IBM Z mainframe environments

passages.text: Timestamps provide a way to confirm the precise time and sequence of events, ensuring the integrity of digital records and preventing disputes.

Time synchronization helps you maintain data integrity by ensuring that timestamps in databases and other storage systems are consistent and accurate. This is essential for data analysis, reporting, and forensic investigations.

concerns.description: Implementation of consistent time synchronization across systems to maintain log integrity and enable event correlation
Protection mechanisms to prevent unauthorized access, modification or deletion of event logs
Implementation of behavioral analytics for detection of anomalous activity across networks and systems
